chats.answer:
For a NAS, you need a portable power station that supports both UPS functionality and USB-based power-failure notification.

The second requirement is the tricky one. Many portable power stations advertise UPS or EPS functionality, but their USB ports are only for charging devices. They cannot tell a Synology, QNAP, or TrueNAS system to shut down when utility power fails.

A suitable unit needs:

UPS/EPS passthrough: Keeps the NAS powered when AC power fails.

USB UPS communication: Reports power status to the NAS, ideally using the standard USB HID UPS protocol.

Automatic shutdown support: Lets the NAS detect an outage and shut down gracefully before the battery runs out.

Automatic recovery: Ideally restores AC output when utility power returns.

Importantly, a USB-C charging port or a USB data port does not automatically mean the station supports NAS shutdown signaling.

Portable power stations worth considering

EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus

Best compact option

286 Wh, 600 W output, under 10 ms transfer, dedicated USB-B UPS communication port. EcoFlow explicitly advertises PC/NAS shutdown functionality. 
EcoFlow US

Caveat: Native Synology/QNAP compatibility isn't guaranteed; NUT or EcoFlow's software may be needed.

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus

Best for longer runtime

1,024 Wh, 10 ms rated transfer, USB-C data communication. Supports USB HID UPS reporting with newer NUT versions.

Caveat: Some Synology systems don't recognize it directly, so a separate NUT server may be necessary.

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra / Ultra Plus

3,072 Wh, under 10 ms transfer, USB-C UPS-HID communication explicitly documented by EcoFlow. 
EcoFlow CA

Caveat: NAS-specific shutdown interoperability still needs testing.

The distinction is important: USB HID support is not the same as proven plug-and-play shutdown on your NAS. Some NAS firmware ships older NUT drivers, and certain EcoFlow implementations have reported low-battery signaling issues.

My recommendation

For a smaller NAS, start with the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus. For a NAS that needs many hours of backup, consider the DELTA 3 Plus. If automatic shutdown must work reliably without custom configuration, a conventional APC or CyberPower USB UPS is still the safer choice.

One question will determine which option actually works for you:

What NAS are you using? For example, Synology DS923+, QNAP TS-464, TrueNAS, or Unraid.

With the exact NAS model, I can narrow this down to units that support its shutdown mechanism, rather than just those advertising USB communication.
